subject: Incident log shelf-life & access controls Q&A
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finbank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Incident: request for retained logs and evidence handling

Hi Vanessa,

We detected suspicious API activity against our tenant last night and our internal SecOps team needs a short forensic package to scope impact. Specifically we need:
- access logs (auth, token issuance) for the 24-hour window starting 2026-05-16T22:00Z
- per-request metadata (request id, model, route, latency) for any requests flagged as anomalous
- KV/prefix cache snapshots if available for the same window

Please confirm:
1) How long does Redwood retain the detailed request logs by default?
2) Can you produce an export with chain-of-custody (checksums and a manifest)?
3) Are there region/residency constraints for the exported package?

We have attached a short evidence request form (forensic-evidence-request.pdf). This is time-sensitive — can you confirm feasibility and an ETA?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Security Operations
FinBank

Attachment: forensic-evidence-request.pdf (application/pdf, 86 KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident: request for retained logs and evidence handling

Hi Ellen — thanks for the details and the form. I can absolutely get this started. High-level answers up front:
1) Default retention: detailed request logs (per-request payload metadata and full headers) are kept for 90 days by default for hosted customers; aggregated metrics are retained longer.
2) Yes — we can produce an export that includes a manifest and SHA256 checksums; our forensics package typically includes an S3 bundle with checksums and a short chain-of-custody note.
3) Region: we can produce the export from the US region where your tenant is hosted. If you require data to remain within a specific sub-region or to be delivered via an air-gapped mechanism, we need to note that in the legal hold.

Next steps: I want to loop in our security lead to confirm we can extend retention beyond 90 days (if needed) and to prepare the preservation hold. Marissa, can you confirm the process and whether we need formal approval for a 180-day hold? Karthik, Im adding you for custody/chain-of-custody details and any additional artifacts we should include (KV cache snapshot procedure).

ETA: If we have a signed evidence request and confirmation of the window, we can produce an initial package (log indexes + manifest) within 24 hours; full raw bundles may take up to 48 hours depending on size.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acknowledged-request-stub.txt (text/plain, 1 KB)

Looping in. High level notes:
- We can approve a preservation hold up to 180 days for customer-facing incidents after sign-off from Legal & CS. For anything longer we need an SOW amendment.
- Please ensure FinBank signs the evidence request form and the data transfer agreement addendum (small doc) before we export.

Karthik, prioritize: what artifacts do you recommend for a first response bundle so the customer can triage quickly? Keep it lean: hashed indexes, per-request metadata CSV, and top 100 anomalous request payloads. If we can include a KV snapshot that would help but confirm feasibility (it can be heavy).

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@finbank.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident: request for retained logs and evidence handling

Ellen / team — technical reply and scope:
- Immediate bundle (ETA ~24 hrs): per-request metadata CSV (request_id, timestamp, route, model, user_id hashed, latency_ms), index with SHA256 checksums, a short readme describing collection times. This will be in a US S3 bucket with presigned links.
- KV cache snapshot: we can attempt a consistent snapshot of active KV caches for the tenant, but that requires a short service quiesce (sub-second to seconds depending on shards). If you need an exact snapshot for forensic replay we should schedule a 5–10 minute window.
- Chain-of-custody: we provide manifest.csv (file, size, SHA256), a signed transfer note (digital signature from our security team), and MD5/SHA hashes in the package. We can also timestamp the manifest with an RFC3339 stamp.

Constraints & ask: please confirm (a) exact UTC window (start/end), (b) point of contact for legal signature (name + email), and (c) whether FinBank requires logs to be redacted prior to export. If redaction is requested, that will add time.

Attachment: sample-kv-cache-logs.tar.gz (application/gzip, 150 MB)

Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
